headline: Revenue slips on disposals, tax swing narrows net loss
summary_short: Liberty Global's Q2 FY2026 revenue fell 7.7% y/y to $1,172.0 million on dispositions and organic softness at Telenet, and the company swung to a $365.1 million net loss after a $198.2 million discrete tax charge and non-deductible FX-related items pushed the effective tax rate to 99.8% YTD.
summary_long: Revenue fell 7.7% y/y ($97.1M), including $51.3M from dispositions; organic revenue was down 6.0% on lower residential fixed subscription revenue (customer losses, ARPU) and softer broadcasting/other revenue at Telenet and VM Ireland. Operating income fell to $3.0M from $29.6M as programming-cost savings were offset by revenue declines. The $365.1M net loss versus a $2,792.9M prior-year loss reflects a much smaller FX/fair-value swing than 2025, though a 99.8% YTD tax rate (a derecognized U.S. tax receivable, non-deductible foreign losses) kept pretax income at -$335.0M. Cash rose to $2,418.6M on $677.8M of EdgeConneX proceeds and $110.7M from the UPC Slovakia sale, against $745.5M of H1 capex. No buybacks occurred (no 2026 program); long-term debt fell 14.7% y/y. No forward guidance was issued.

The 99.8% YTD effective tax rate is a one-off driven by the Q1 2026 derecognition of a ~$133.3M U.S. tax-litigation refund receivable following an adverse Tenth Circuit appellate ruling, plus non-deductible FX/investment losses in the U.K./Netherlands/Luxembourg — not a run-rate figure. Segment revenue at the 50%-owned VMO2 JV and VodafoneZiggo JV (equity-method, not consolidated) is disclosed in the MD&A but excluded from these consolidated KPIs, consistent with the shard's basis. y/y deltas for EBIT, EPS, net income and pretax income (all negative-to-less-negative, no sign flip) are expressed as loss-narrowing magnitude — e.g. net income '+86.9% y/y' means the loss shrank from -$2,792.9M to -$365.1M, computed as (|prior|-|current|)/|prior| — not the raw signed (current-prior)/prior formula, which would misleadingly read as a decline.

drivers.explanation: Decline driven by $51.3M from dispositions (UPC Slovakia) plus organic softness: residential fixed subscription revenue fell on lower customer counts and ARPU at Telenet, and other/broadcasting revenue declined at Telenet and VM Ireland.
Programming and other direct costs fell 19.3% (lower content costs, Formula E event costs), partly offsetting the revenue decline, but not enough to hold gross profit flat given the disposition drag.
Fell to $3.0M from $29.6M as revenue and gross-profit declines outpaced cost savings in programming and other direct costs.
Narrower loss y/y mainly reflects 2025's outsized foreign currency transaction loss ($2,089.9M) not recurring, versus a much smaller FX loss this quarter, despite a higher effective tax rate.
Improved y/y for the same reason as net income — the prior year's large FX transaction loss dominated pretax results and did not repeat at the same scale in 2026.
Cash rose on $677.8M of proceeds from the sale of the EdgeConneX investment and $110.7M from the UPC Slovakia disposal, exceeding capex and debt-repayment outflows.

Quarter marked by a 99.8% YTD effective tax rate from a derecognized U.S. tax-litigation receivable and non-deductible foreign losses; no share repurchase program is authorized for 2026, and the filing states no numeric forward guidance.
